character: Sam, a fictional Kiwi site manager (late 30s to 40s), the 'Sam' in the email and 'Sam K.' in the daily log. General urban New Zealand accent (Auckland or Wellington), not broad, not Australian. Dry, low and a bit sheepish: this is a confession to a mate in the site office, not a performance, so the joke is on the speaker, never on other site managers. The diary lines are read flat with a natural downstep (Monday a full sentence, Wednesday flatter, 'Ditto' the flattest). The product lines are the same person, a touch more awake, still with no announcer lift and no tagline cadence. Sam never says he uses QSME or that it saved him anything: product lines are plain instructions and observations, never a testimonial. It's an AI voice, so it never speaks as the founder and never says 'we built'. QSME is said only in the CTA, as 'Q-S-me' (kyoo-ess-mee). Casting: the same Kiwi QS voice as 'Six bids', 'Column H' and 'Day 23' (shortlist Arnold bISW1PJRBPT7aRbtPJlB, James QlZn2MPaf2jDn0461bnj), or an A/B with a Kiwi woman's voice (Sam works either way).
casting_line: Confession. Site diary gets done Friday afternoon. Wednesday gets as above. Ditto.
continuous_read_v2:
Confession. Site diary gets done Friday afternoon.

Monday gets a paragraph.

Wednesday gets as above.

Ditto.

Nine months later.

It was. I think.

Log the rain day once.

It's already in the diary.

Photos land on the day you post them.

Not on Friday.

It writes the bits you'd forget by Friday.

Book a thirty-minute demo at Q-S-me dot build.

post_processing: Primary source: render continuous_read_v2 three times on the chosen voice, slice it and place each piece at its start_s. Lines 02 to 04 must come from one take (a natural downstep through the week). Use per-line renders only as patches, with previous_text/next_text so the intonation carries over. Keep the least polished take.
Room tone bed: 60 s of a real quiet site office (fridge hum, distant traffic) recorded on a phone, under the whole 29.25 s at about -50 dBFS so silences never drop to digital zero.
EQ for a phone voice memo: high-pass 90 Hz, -2 dB shelf above 10 kHz, light de-ess. Compression 2:1 to 3:1, 3 to 4 dB GR. VO about -16 LUFS short-term; master -14 LUFS integrated, -1 dBTP. No reverb.

SFX synced to picture, ducked 10 to 12 dB under any word they overlap: pen scratch 0.0 to 2.36, 4.4 to 5.0, 6.15 to 6.5, 6.7 to 7.0, 7.7 to 7.95 (harder, 'Ditto'), ditto-mark ticks 6.05, 6.6 and 7.1, underline flick 7.95 to 8.08; a kettle clicking off at 1.6; rain on a tin roof 4.15 to 5.95 (fade in and out over 0.2 s); a low soft hit on 'Nine months later.' 8.5; one generic mail chime 9.5 (nothing that sounds like Outlook or Gmail); marker squeaks 11.92 to 12.32 (the ring) and 12.3 to 12.5 (the '?'); soft thuds on 'It was.' 12.05 and 'Probably.' 12.55; swipe whoosh 13.3 to 13.6; trackpad clicks 13.85, 14.36, 15.2, 19.24, 19.68; soft ticks as the log entries write in 16.68 and 16.9; a light pop as the proof-of-work entry lands in the log 20.0; phone taps 21.38 and 21.8; a soft camera shutter 21.96; swipe 22.9 to 23.2; paper slide 23.1. No OS-branded sounds.
Music: none under the skit (0 to 13.3). Enters on the swipe into QSME at 13.3, sits about 18 dB under the VO, dips for the shutter at 21.96 and resolves on one held chord at about 29.05.
Never time-stretch more than about 4%; if a take runs past max_s, use another take.
Bounce a mono VO stem and mux it onto outputs/as-above-4x5.mp4 with tools/mux as a separate track. If the 9:16 cut is built later on the same timeline, the same stem fits it.
